summary: Hold: 2.0.10 is MIT, zero-dependency and free of known advisories, but it has had no release since 2023-07-11, carries no npm provenance, and the legacy browser baseline and actual plugin usage are unrecorded, so the existing pinned version can stay in place while a suite-level keep/upgrade/replace decision is made, but it should not be adopted for new work.
reasoning: The 12-month release-recency constraint is not met: 2.0.10 is the latest of 27 published versions and was published 2023-07-11, while the registry record was last modified 2026-09-21 and the repository was pushed 2026-10-23. Repository activity is not a release of this package, so this is treated as a hard constraint failure that caps the verdict at hold regardless of the score.

Zero runtime dependencies and an empty dependencies object; the only coupling is the peer dependency @antv/x6 ^2.x, which ties this plugin to the sibling X6 core package and means it cannot be judged or replaced independently of that renderer.
Security posture is otherwise clean: the dossier records no advisories, the license is MIT, there are no install scripts, and the package is not deprecated.

No npm attestation exists for the published tarball and the dossier contains no evidence of a CI publish workflow. The requirement allows this gap only if exact versions are pinned and the gap is recorded, which is the mitigation carried in the caveats.
Bundled TypeScript declarations and dual CJS/ESM output reduce integration risk in an existing application and preserve the existing build baseline options.

Fit cannot be confirmed from measurements: the dossier does not record the legacy application's browser/runtime baseline, nor whether the legacy code actually uses this plugin, so the requirement's compatibility and behaviour-preservation constraints are unverified rather than satisfied.
Footprint is small: no runtime dependencies, 288 KB unpacked, MIT; install size was not measured, so the full on-disk cost is unknown.
3,760 weekly downloads and 156 open upstream issues indicate a small but non-zero user base; upstream issue triage is not evidence that this specific plugin is maintained.
The named alternative, D3, is not assessed in this dossier, and nothing in the dossier shows that a lower-level renderer could reproduce this plugin's existing integrated behaviour.
caveats: No npm provenance: pin 2.0.10 exactly, install from the registry tarball, and record the provenance gap in the suite decision, as the requirement allows.
No release since 2023-07-11. The plugin line has been effectively frozen for over three years even though the monorepo is active, so fixes for this package may never ship.
If the legacy app moves to a newer X6 major, this 2.0.10 pin is only declared compatible with @antv/x6 ^2.x and may not upgrade with the core.
The legacy browser/runtime baseline was not recorded, so compatibility with the existing application cannot be judged from this dossier.
The dossier does not record whether the legacy app still uses the scroller plugin, so the cost of keeping it is unknown and the actual usage must be confirmed before a migration decision.
Install size was not measured; only the 288 KB unpacked figure is known.
64 npm maintainer accounts are an org-level publish permission, not a guarantee that any one person maintains this plugin; 156 upstream issues remain open.
